Dominant approaches: BM25 baseline, dense retrieval (ColBERT, BERT-based), co-citation analysis, temporal decay weighting (uniform or adaptive), stochastic selection with temporal decay.

Common assumptions: Temporal proximity correlates with relevance; temporal decay can mitigate drift; version timestamps are available; semantic similarity can be combined with temporal signal.

Datasets: UA-StatuteRetrieval, Goodreads Poetry, Korean QA dataset, AlpacaEval, Arena-Hard, MMLU, etc., Synthea EHR, Wikipedia.

Benchmarks: Various retrieval benchmarks (co-citation MRR, Hit@k), QA metrics (Exact Match, F1), recommendation metrics (Catalog Coverage, Recall).

Metrics: MRR, Hit@k, Exact Match, F1, Catalog Coverage, Recall, Gini-index, Novelty, AlpacaEval score, etc.

Limitations repeated: Lack of end-to-end QA evaluation, focus on proxy tasks, limited to specific domains/languages, not addressing versioned textual documents, not proposing mitigation strategies.

Underexplored combinations: Temporal relevance weighting combined with dense retrievers for QA over versioned regulatory texts; benchmarking temporal QA on statutes/policies; hybrid graph-text temporal retrieval for legal.

Contradictions: Maybe none directly, but some papers show uniform decay performs poorly (arxiv:2604.26970) while others use uniform temporal decay weighting (doi:10.33480/jitk.v12i1.8240) - not a contradiction but different findings.
